gen-gf-oxanium-fs-karma: Unbroken drafting-pen lines give Oxanium its commanding look, with curves that end in clear daylight. And Karma, a serif, thins its horizontals slightly against the verticals, for a trustworthy, classic feel.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Oxanium keeps a tube-like thickness through every bend, its lowercase looking big and its curves ending in clear daylight. Noto Sans Thaana feels approachable beside it, with wide channels into each counter.
gen-gf-palanquin-dark-fs-literata: Barely any stroke variation marks Palanquin Dark, which feels approachable and modern, while Literata, a serif, shows light but visible modulation. Flat modern lines meet a sophisticated, bookish voice.
gen-gf-paprika-fs-quicksand: Scattered, capital-sized lowercase gives Paprika its commanding look. Quicksand then settles things down with round, bulb-like bowls and bars of identical thickness, so the display shouts and the text just talks.
gen-gf-paprika-fs-ranade: Counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open give Paprika a commanding, expressive voice. Ranade, a sans-serif, is the quiet partner, its weight shifting only slightly across a spread-out line.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-cossette-titre: Paprika scatters its letters at a distance, with lowercase that fills the line like capitals. And Cossette Titre, a sans-serif, reads close and contemporary, its open bowls welcoming the eye line after line.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-lisu-bosa: Paprika arrives loud, with its letters scattered at a distance. Lisu Bosa then supplies editorial steadiness, its counters spilling into the surrounding space and its tempered contrast like a lightly flexed spring wire.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-newa: Loud, scattered and capital-like, Paprika lets its lowercase fill the line and its counters breathe. But Noto Sans Newa, a sans, keeps things modern, with a clearly open mouth on its lowercase e.
gen-gf-patrick-hand-sc-fs-rowan: Relaxed, Patrick Hand SC keeps a level, unaccented beat. Rowan, a serif, adds generous curves and a gentle thick-thin difference, and feels most comfortable taken a bit at a time.
gen-gf-play-fs-karma: Play has a tall middle band and soft contrast in every curve. Karma, a text serif, takes over with classic, trustworthy forms whose terminals finish well away from the stem.
